newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Greenfields to proceed with fund raising.
newsitem.headline: Greenfields to proceed with fund raising.

text.p: Takeover target Greenfields Coal Company Ltd said on Wednesday its fund raising plans would proceed with two share issues and a debt raising.
Mineral Resources Corp (MRC) of Canada is offering one of its shares for every eight Greenfields shares, a bid Greenfields directors have rejected as unwelcome and too low.

The company said a one for five non-renounceable issue at 26 cents with a bonus share announced on July 15 would go ahead, as would a capital reconstruction consisting of a two into one consolidation and the issue of 50 million ordinary shares at 20 cents par value to be sold by a trustee to benefit the company.
Greenfields also said it would seek debt financing after the refusal of the Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) to grant a waiver to rules governing the issue of shares during a takeover bid.
Discussions were under way with a party that had previously planned to take a private placement of 10.17 million preference shares, Greenfields said.

"Our appeal (against the ASX's refusal) goes up on Friday," a company spokesman said. "We are keen to do (the placement) but if we can't do it the group who were going to take that 10 percent have said they will lend a similar amount to the company," the spokesman said.
He declined to identify the potential lender.
"It is a major Australian group who at this stage are indicating they would be prepared to try to get up to 20 percent of the company," the spokesman said.
Greenfields said the complete capital raising would exceed A$14 million which would provide funding to its U.S. projects including payment of all existing debt.

Greenfields shares were reinstated to trading but by 10.25 a.m. (0025 GMT) no stock had changed hands. The shares were quoted with bid at 10 cents and an ask of 18.5 cents compared to a last trade on July 18 of 18.5 cents.
